'Abysmal' polling looms over Trump's 'big day' at the UN: 'Hail Mary diplomacy?' President Donald Trump is set to address the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday as public support collapses for his handling of foreign policy.Only 36 percent of Americans believe the U.S. is winning the war, compared with 64 percent who say it is not,according to a CNN poll conducted last week, and White House reporter Alayna Treene noted that only 29 percent of Americans approve of how Trump is handling foreign affairs broadly, versus 71 percent who disapprove."These are just abysmal poll numbers when it comes to foreignpolicy," Treene said, adding that she expects the numbers to loom over the president's remarks even as he tries to use the speech to reshape his image on the world stage."It's a big day for thepresident," agreed "CNN News Central" anchor John Berman, "but he's facing someserious, serious headwinds interms of what the Americanpeople think."Treene said she had been told by U.N.
